title: Turrican II: The Final Fight
build: Triangle disk release from the C64Games archive

records.c: Type three reserves a second slot and initializes two horizontally adjacent pieces with shared health $20. The source controller handles contact and weapon hits on either piece, entry animation, an eight-pose idle cycle and a delayed burst of seven type-four actors. Both linked pieces explode on destruction with 1500 points; bounds release the pair.
Operand byte 1 of the BPL instruction at $6C02, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.
Operand byte 2 of the JSR instruction at $6C04, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.

Restore both piece colours, test player contact and character damage on either shape, then update entry/idle animation or timed burst allocation. The passive partner has state zero and returns immediately.
Seven entry shapes for the controller; partner uses each selected shape plus one.
Seven per-pose entry delays, read by the decreasing index.
Eight looping idle shapes; partner uses each plus one.
Eight signed X increments selected by timer bits.

Type four starts with health two, rises with stored X/upward velocities until its upper terrain probe is solid, waits for horizontal player proximity, then falls four pixels per update. Ground contact changes its animation and sound, and the final pose releases it. Shared contact/weapon/flash destruction requests 200 points.
Six looping shapes for the rising/falling child.

Type five reserves two linked lower pieces and initializes the controller with health $20. It periodically faces the player, animates lower shapes forward/backward with movement sound, tests a four-row two-cell damage window and shares hit colours with its parts. Terrain probes stop horizontal movement or initiate a fourteen-entry falling curve; position updates keep both lower pieces attached. Destruction requests 2000 points.

On an eleven-call divider face the player and choose signed X direction. Restore piece colours, test contact and scan up to four screen rows for weapon characters. Counter underflow or shared flash explodes all pieces; otherwise move along terrain while maintaining linked positions.

Cycle the lower piece's shapes in facing-dependent order with sound. Probe terrain ahead, update signed X and linked positions, bob the controller through seven XOR entries and select falling when the support probe is clear.
Use a fourteen-entry signed Y curve until terrain is found, then snap the controller Y and return to walking. Update both lower pieces twenty-one pixels below and reverse direction on a side probe.

Three initial piece colours.
Controller state one and two passive state-zero pieces.

Three relative pixel Y offsets.
Seven XOR values applied to the controller Y during motion.
Fourteen signed Y increments indexed by the decreasing falling timer.

Type six has a stationary parent and moving child states. Initialize subtype shape, colour, health, vertical offset and a twenty-one-entry flight curve. The parent animates to a terminal pose, waits and allocates one moving child. The child approaches the player and changes to an attack curve near the target. Contact in attack state attaches it to the player, deals damage on a two-call divider and requires twelve joystick-direction changes before release into another movement state.

Apply subtype colour and contact rules, indexed character damage and flash destruction. Ordinary low subtypes damage on contact; attack state two instead advances to attached state three. Surviving hits flash and destruction requests subtype-selected BCD scores.

Choose facing toward the player, move by signed X and the initial curve, then alternate facing animation until within the selected distance. Start attack state two with a reloaded twenty-one-entry curve.

State three follows player X/Y with facing offsets, applies player damage on a two-call divider and decrements its release counter only when the joystick's low-nibble direction changes. Twelve changes advance it out of attached state. Other non-parent states use the attack flight path.
Two initialization shapes for parent and child.
Five state-selected colours for parent, approaching, attack, attached and released movement.
Two initialization health values for the parent/child subtypes.
Five state-selected BCD score additions; also read by the hidden spawner destruction path.

Type seven initializes a hidden controller with health ten and subtype-selected child direction. Periodic timer-derived delays allocate moving type-seven children with zero health, a sixteen-shape animation and a selected forty-entry Y curve. Child terrain collision after its short initial guard destroys it; shared contact/weapon/flash handling applies to both states.

State zero counts down and allocates a randomized child, selecting curve index, animation phase and signed direction. State one cycles sixteen shapes, moves horizontally by its direction and vertically by the forty-entry curve, then tests terrain after the guard ends.
Two signed horizontal steps chosen by subtype.
Forty signed Y increments shared by flying children and bouncing actors; selected starting indices change their path segment.

Type eight initializes health two, facing and a forty-entry vertical curve. Move horizontally until side terrain reverses facing. Upward terrain reloads a curve index and sound; downward terrain switches to a seven-pose landing animation before resuming motion. Shared damage or flash destruction requests 250 points.
Two signed half-pixel X steps.
Seven shapes read by the decreasing landing animation index.

Type nine animates thirteen facing-selected poses. Player contact during selected open shapes attempts to reserve two additional type-nine slots, hides the ordinary player and enters a capture animation. Captured animation updates the two added shapes and their attached Y positions, then releases all three actor slots. Protected/wheel contact instead explodes the source with 100 points. A failed allocation can leave the first reserved piece; no visible consequence is established.

State one advances on an eleven-call divider, hiding the source at its terminal pose and selecting one of five shapes for the two captured-player pieces. Their Y alternates by XOR four; after the five entries end, release both pieces and source.
Thirteen animation shapes for the first facing.
Thirteen animation shapes for the second facing.
Five shapes for the first of the two captured-player pieces in one facing. The second piece uses the next shape except for $FE.
Five corresponding captured-piece shapes for the other facing.

Type ten starts closed in state fourteen. A first weapon hit opens it to state fifteen. Subsequent hits decrement a five-call divider and advance a shared damage/contact cycle counter; deep player contact uses the same cycle path. Each surviving cycle emits a type-ten particle when a slot is free. End of the cycle counter clears support flags, explodes the source and requests 5000 points. Per-slot standing/deeper-contact flags aggregate into resident bytes $62/$63.

Aggregate all eleven support flags, service the nine-entry bump curve and test player contact. Near-top contact adjusts player Y and sets its support flag. Deeper contact starts bump/sound and enters the cycle counter path; no contact clears both flags for this slot.

Move a child with its signed horizontal speed, reversing on bounds or terrain, and follow a thirty-one-entry Y curve. Terrain, curve limit or bounds changes it to resident effect type two with a negative state. The horizontal terrain sample's side selector reads the unindexed first slot speed at $BC6C, while actual motion uses this slot's indexed speed; the visible consequence remains open.
Nine signed Y increments for the support contact bump.

Thirty authored signed Y increments. The preliminary lookup can index thirty and read the following $AD opcode at $7A63; the later limit test ends the particle before applying that entry. The final indexed entry aliases the $AD opcode at $7A63; keep that address typed as code.

Unless halted, rotate the environment through a nine-entry direction table. On an eleven-call divider alternate two four-glyph frames at $C350. Near the top camera area, reload a mutable actor-record type when no type-ten actor is active. At the selected player Y threshold install automatic upward departure and select the facing-dependent player shape. The preliminary particle-curve lookup also reads this first $AD opcode at index thirty; a read watchpoint confirmed it, and the later limit test ends the particle before applying that candidate increment.

Move player Y upward two pixels until it passes $0C, then jump to the resident next-level transition.
Rotate eight separate eight-byte glyph columns upward by two bytes, saving fourteen stack bytes plus the first byte in Y and restoring each column's wrapped pair.
Rotate all eight glyph columns downward by two bytes, preserving their wrapped pairs on the stack and in Y.
Rotate each of eight eight-byte rows left across the eight character columns through carry, wrapping the outgoing bit into the final column.
Rotate the eight-column rows right through carry, wrapping back into the first column.
Apply horizontal left rotation then the upward column rotation.
Apply left rotation then the downward column rotation.
Apply right rotation then the upward column rotation.
Apply right rotation then the downward column rotation.
Nine low bytes for neutral and eight direction-selected glyph rotations.
Nine corresponding high bytes.
Animated glyph frame at $7CBB-$7CBB. Two-frame alternating index.
Animated glyph divider at $7CBC-$7CBC. Eleven-call divider for the alternating four-glyph pattern.
Animated glyph frame ends at $7CBD-$7CBE. Last-byte offsets thirty-one and sixty-three selecting the frames backwards.
Animated glyph frame zero at $7CBF-$7CDE. Thirty-two bitmap bytes copied to $C350 for frame zero.
Animated glyph frame one at $7CDF-$7CFE. Thirty-two bitmap bytes copied to $C350 for frame one.
